tutorials.title: Battery draining too quickly

steps.text:
If you're experience issues with your iPhone's battery, there are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot the problem.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Check for iOS updates
Check your battery insights
Adjust your iPhone's brightness
Ensure you're using Wi-Fi or LTE where possible
Enable Low Power Mode
Contact Apple for a battery replacement

steps.heading: Check for iOS updates
steps.text: To start, make sure your iPhone is running the latest version of iOS. This may help resolve any issues you're experiencing. You'll also need iOS 26 or later to view your device's Daily Usage chart and use its Adaptive Power feature to help extend your iPhone's battery life.
links: Checking for and installing system updates

steps.heading: Check your battery insights
steps.text:
Next, open up Settings and tap Battery. Your iPhone will give you suggestions, if there are any, right above your Daily Usage chart.
On this screen, you'll also be able to see how much battery you've used throughout the day, and which apps are using up more battery life than others.
At the bottom, you can tap on Battery Health to view that, as well as your iPhone's maximum estimated capacity and the total number of battery cycles your iPhone has used.
Tap on Charging, and you'll be able to set a charge limit for your device (to promote longevity at the cost of overall daily capacity), or simply enable battery-optimized charging.
Tap on Power Mode, and you'll be able to adjust automatic features that attempt to extend your iPhone's overall uptime when your battery is low.
links: Managing your iPhone battery

steps.heading: Adjusting your iPhone's brightness
steps.text:
Consider enabling auto-brightness, which can help your iPhone preserve battery life by automatically adjusting your screen's brightness as needed.
Similarly, you can also enable auto-lock to prevent your iPhone from staying idle for long periods of time and draining the battery.
links: Changing your auto-lock and brightness preferences
options: Next: Using Wi-Fi or LTE wherever possible

steps.heading: Using Wi-Fi or LTE wherever possible
steps.text:
Wi-Fi uses less power than cellular networks, so make sure you're connecting to a nearby Wi-Fi network with a good signal whenever possible. Your iPhone may use more battery than expected if you're in an area with a poor signal strength (for Wi-Fi or cellular).
Additionally, iPhone 12 models (or later) allow come with a 5G Auto feature, found within the Cellular Data Options section of your Cellular settings, which will allow your iPhone to automatically switch to LTE if you wouldn't be getting any better speeds on a 5G connection (saving battery life).
links: Turning your Wi-Fi on and off

steps.heading: Enabling Low Power Mode
steps.text: If you're running low on battery and you need as much uptime on your iPhone as possible, open up the Control Center and tap on the battery icon to enable Low Power Mode. It's a temporary solution that will disable various settings and features to give you as much extra battery life as possible.
links: Using Control Center
options: Next: Contacting Apple for a battery replacement

steps.heading: Contacting Apple for a battery replacement
steps.text:
If you're still encountering issues with your battery, and that hasn't been resolved by any of the previous steps, restarting your iPhone, or using different cables to charge your device, you may need to set up a service appointment at an Apple Genius Bar or other Authorized Service Provider.
Similarly, if your iPhone is reporting an issue with your Battery Health, or your iPhone is recommending service for your battery, you'll want to consider replacing your battery to restore your device's performance and total capacity.

tutorials.title: Can't make or receive calls
tutorials.intro: Not being able to make or answer calls leaves you cut off from important contacts and emergency services. Checking your network connection and SIM settings helps fix dropped calls and gets your phone working normally again.

steps.text:
If you're unable to make phone calls on your iPhone, there are a few steps you can take to determine if your issue is with your device or with your carrier (and if this is a temporary problem or a permanent situation you're encountering).
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Check your existing connection
Use Airplane Mode to "reset" your connection
Check for iOS updates
Restart your iPhone
Reset your network settings
Set a default number for your Dual-SIM setup (if applicable)
Find additional support to address your problem
options: Next: Check your cellular or Wi-Fi signal

steps.heading: Check your connection
steps.text:
Check the cellular signal status icon in the upper-right corner of your device. Generally, the more bars that are displayed, the better the connection; if you have low or no signal, that may be the reason why you're experiencing issues making phone calls.
If you're connected to Wi-Fi, you'll also be able to view your signal strength in the same area. Enabling Wi-Fi calling may help you place phone calls in areas with limited or no cellular coverage.

steps.heading: Use Airplane Mode to "reset" your connection
steps.text:
It's possible that your device may have a great connection to a nearby cellular tower or Wi-Fi access point, but you still can't make a phone call.
You can try switching your phone to Airplane Mode, waiting approximately 15 seconds, and turning Airplane Mode off again.
If you're still unable to make a call, this typically means there is a problem with the hardware your device is connecting to. You can confirm this by checking if your device can make phone calls at a different location.
links: Turning Airplane Mode on and off

steps.heading: Check for iOS updates
steps.text: You'll want to make sure your iPhone is running the latest version of iOS. You'll also want to check to see if you have any pending carrier settings updates to install.
links: Checking for and installing system updates

steps.heading: Try restarting your iPhone
steps.text: Manually restarting your iPhone may help solve any connectivity issues you're experiencing. It's a great "first-step" troubleshooting technique for most issues you encounter on your device.
links: Powering your iPhone on and off

steps.heading: Reset your network settings
steps.text:
Resetting your network settings will erase previously used settings like your Wi-Fi passwords, preferred networks, and VPN and APN settings.
You'll be able to resync your Wi-Fi passwords from iCloud, but the other settings will need to be entered again.
If you had to enter APN settings manually to access a cellular network, you'll need to do that again before attempting a phone call.
links: Resetting your iPhone’s Settings and Network Settings

steps.heading: Using the right SIM in a Dual-SIM configuration
steps.text: If you're using two SIMs in your device, otherwise known as a Dual-SIM setup, check to make sure that your device is using the correct, intended SIM for calls. It's possible that your default SIM has a weak connection to your carrier, which you may be able to get around by switching to the other SIM.
links: Set your default SIM for calls, texts, and cellular data

steps.heading: Get additional support
steps.text:
If you're still having issues making a phone call on your iPhone, you should contact your carrier for additional support. They'll be able to help identify if there is an issue on their end that's affecting your calls (e.g. a problem with your account, your SIM, or even a local cellular tower).
It's also possible that your device may be experiencing a hardware issue. If so, you'll want to contact Apple to set up an appointment at a local Genius Bar or authorized support center.

tutorials.title: Personal Hotspot isn't working
tutorials.intro: Learn how to fix a personal hotspot that won’t connect. Follow this step-by-step user manual to troubleshoot connection drops, password issues, and cellular data errors.

steps.text:
The Personal Hotspot feature allows you to broadcast a Wi-Fi network from your iPhone. When other device connect to it, they'll use your iPhone's cellular connection to connect to the internet.
If you're having issues setting up or using Personal Hotspot, there are a few ways you can troubleshoot the issue.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Set up and check Personal Hotspot
Restart your iPhone
Check for iOS updates
Check your cellular connection
Reset your network settings
Change your iPhone's name

steps.heading: Setting up Personal Hotspot
steps.text:
Take a moment to check that Personal Hotspot is enabled on your device. You'll also want to confirm that your carrier and service plan supports Wi-Fi hotspots, or else the feature may not appear (or you may not be able to enable it).
When setting up your Personal Hotspot:
Make sure that you've turned on the "Allow Others to Join" option.
Make sure Cellular Data is enabled via Settings > Cellular
If you're using an iPhone 12 model or later, you can try enabling "Maximum Compatibility" when turning on your iPhone's personal hotspot. (You may need to turn your other devices' Wi-Fi on and off before you can successfully connect to your iPhone's Personal Hotspot.)
You can also try forgetting your Wi-Fi network on your connecting device and reconnecting to your Personal Hotspot, in case you accidentally saved an incorrect password or are encountering some other kind of connection issue.
links: Turning on and managing your personal hotspot's settings

steps.heading: Try restarting your iPhone
steps.text: Manually restarting your iPhone may help solve any issues you're experiencing with your Personal Hotspot. It's a great "first-step" troubleshooting technique for most issues you encounter on your device.
links: Powering your iPhone on and off

steps.heading: Check for iOS updates
steps.text: Make sure your iPhone is running the latest version of iOS, just in case that's somehow preventing you from using the Personal Hotspot feature.
links: Checking for and installing system updates

steps.heading: Checking your cellular connection
steps.text:
It's possible that devices can connect to your Personal Hotspot, but you have a weak or problematic cellular connection that's affecting your devices' performance.
Try turning off your Personal Hotspot temporarily and use your iPhone as you normally would. Make sure you're not connected to a Wi-Fi network and try placing a call or loading a webpage.
If you're encountering issues, try switching your phone to Airplane Mode, waiting 15 seconds, and turning it off. Otherwise, try moving to a location with a stronger or more consistent cellular signal and testing Personal Hotspot again to see if the issue is with your iPhone's connection or the hotspot.

steps.heading: Reset your network settings
steps.text:
Resetting your network settings will erase previously used settings like your Wi-Fi passwords, preferred networks, and VPN and APN settings.
You'll be able to resync your Wi-Fi passwords from iCloud, but the other settings will need to be entered again.
Once you've done this, reboot your device and try re-enabling Personal Hotspot.
links: Resetting your iPhone’s Settings and Network Settings

steps.heading: Changing your iPhone's name
steps.text:
Disable your Personal Hotspot if it's turned on, then try changing your iPhone's name.
Next, enable Airplane Mode, wait 15 seconds, then disable it. Then, try setting up Personal Hotspot again and connecting to it from another nearby device.
links: Changing your iPhone's name

When you enable Wi-Fi Calling, you'll likely be prompted to enter your permanent address. If you can't do this within your iPhone's interface, check to see if you need to do this within your carrier's account settings (on its website or mobile app).
To test if Wi-Fi calling works, simply enable Airplane Mode on your iPhone and attempt to make a phone call while connected to a Wi-Fi network.

steps.heading: Check for iOS updates

Switch to a different Wi-Fi network, ideally at a different location than where you're experiencing issues, and check to see if you can place a call using Wi-Fi Calling. You may need to toggle the feature off, then on again, when testing.

tutorials.title: Wi-Fi connection issues or slowdowns

steps.text:
If you're having issues connecting to a Wi-Fi network, or are experiencing slow Wi-Fi speeds on your iPhone, there are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot the issue.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Confirm your Wi-Fi connection
Turn off Connectivity Assist
Restart your iPhone
Remove VPN profiles
Test your connection with other devices
Reset your network settings

steps.heading: Confirming your Wi-Fi connection
steps.text:
Within the Settings app, take a moment to confirm that your iPhone is connected to a Wi-Fi network. A blue checkmark will appear next to your active connection within your Wi-Fi settings. If you don't see one, tap on an available Wi-Fi network and attempt to connect. (Make sure your iPhone's Airplane Mode isn't on.)
Note: If you're successfully connected to Wi-Fi, but you're getting a "No Internet Connection" message, there may be an issue with your Wi-Fi router/gateway that you'll need to troubleshoot. Apple also maintains a list of recommended settings for Wi-Fi routers you'll want to review.
links: Turning your Wi-Fi on and off

steps.heading: Turning off Connectivity Assist
steps.text: Try turning off Connectivity Assist, as your iPhone might be trying to use a connection from a nearby cellular network instead of your Wi-Fi connection.
links: Turning Wi-Fi assist off

steps.heading: Try restarting your iPhone
steps.text: Manually restarting your iPhone may help solve any issues you're experiencing with Wi-Fi Calling. It's a great "first-step" troubleshooting technique for most issues you encounter on your device.
links: Powering your iPhone on and off
options: Next: Removing VPN profiles or related security apps

steps.heading: Removing VPN profiles or related security apps
steps.text:
It's possible that a VPN profile, or a security-themed app you've installed, is interfering with your connection. Try removing any VPN profiles within your Settings app's "VPN & Device Management" section, restart your iPhone, and try connecting to a nearby Wi-Fi network and using your device as you normally would.
If you're required to use a VPN — for example, to access resources for your job — you may need to talk to your VPN manager to figure out a solution for any connection issues you're experiencing.
Similarly, you may have installed a security-themed app on your iPhone that is somehow interfering with your network connection. Look for these, remove them, and see if that improves your experience. It's possible that you may be able to reinstall them and adjust their settings to fix your issue, if you've isolated your connection problems to a particular app.
links: Deleting an app

steps.heading: Try connecting with another device
steps.text:
From the same spot you're attempting to use Wi-Fi on your iPhone, try connecting to the same network on another device (such as an iPad, a laptop, another phone, et cetera). If you can connect and transfer data without issue, your router and network are likely configured correctly.
If you're still experiencing issues, you may be at the limit of the Wi-Fi network's range, or you may need to split your single Wi-Fi network into a Wi-Fi network on 2.4GHz and a Wi-Fi network on 5GHz, then use whichever gives you the best connection manually.
You can also try restarting your Wi-Fi router or cable modem, if applicable, to see if that helps. You should also check to see if your Wi-Fi router has any firmware updates, which may alleviate any issues you're experiencing.

steps.heading: Reset your network settings
steps.text:
Resetting your network settings will erase previously used settings like your Wi-Fi passwords, preferred networks, and VPN and APN settings.
You'll be able to resync your Wi-Fi passwords from iCloud, but the other settings will need to be entered again.
Once you've done this, reboot your device, connect to your Wi-Fi network, and check to see if your connection issues are fixed.
If you're still having connection problems, or if your iPhone can't connect to any Wi-Fi networks successfully, you may need to contact Apple for service.
links: Resetting your iPhone’s Settings and Network Settings

steps.heading: Powering off my iPhone
steps.text:
Normally, you'd power off your iPhone by:
iPhone with Home button: Holding the iPhone's side button until the on-screen Power Off slider appears
iPhone without Home button: Holding the iPhone's side button and one of the two volume buttons until the on-screen Power Off slider appears
You can also turn off your iPhone by swiping down from the upper-right corner to load the Control Center, and then tapping on the power icon in the upper-right corner. There's also a "Shut Down" option you can tap under Settings > General.
If you're still encountering issues, or you can't load any of these options, you can also try force-restarting your iPhone.
links: Powering your iPhone on and off

steps.heading: Force-restarting your iPhone
steps.text:
If you can't power off your iPhone normally, or it's otherwise unresponsive, try force-restarting it:
iPhone with Face ID
Press and quickly release the volume up button
Press and quickly release the volume down button
Press and hold the side button
When you see the Apple logo, release the side button.
iPhone 7 or 7 Plus
Press and hold the side button and the volume down button until you see the Apple logo (approximately 10 seconds).
iPhone 6s or earlier
Press and hold the Home button and the side or top button until you see the Apple logo (approximately 10 seconds).

If a passcode has been setup and enabled on your current iPhone, you will be prompted to enter that passcode on your new iPhone.

steps.text: Tap Learn More to view Apple’s data-collection and privacy policies, including information about how your information is shared and stored. Otherwise, tap Continue to proceed.

Tap Continue and follow the instructions to set up Face ID on your new iPhone, an important authentication system that increases your device’s security. Once complete, you’ll be able to use Face ID to unlock your iPhone, confirm purchases, and sign into websites (on Safari).

Note: 

If the information you would like to be transferred onto your new iPhone has been previously backed up to your Apple account's iCloud, or you want to transfer from a different device source, tap Other Options to select a different method on a later step.

steps.text: You will then be asked to agree to Apple’s Terms and Conditions to continue setup.
Tap Customize to proceed.
notes:

steps.text: Tap Continue.

If you previously signed into an Apple ID during the iPhone setup process, you’ll be able to tap Continue to set up Apple Pay, which allows you to link your debit or credit cards to your iPhone. You can then use your iPhone to pay for digital and physical items or transfer money to your contacts.
Tap Continue to setup Screen time.
notes:
Note: 

Screen Time, which helps you keep track of your iPhone use, set time limits for apps, or limit the apps and contacts you can interact with between set times during the day. If you’re using iOS' Family Sharing features, you can also set limits for your kids' devices.

steps.text: Tap Continue.

notes:
Note: 

If your device supports these features, you'll then receive similar prompts to set up Apple Intelligence, Camera Control, and Action Button.

tutorials.title: Troubleshooting why my phone won't turn on or off
tutorials.intro: Learn how to troubleshoot a smartphone that won't turn on, turn off, or is completely unresponsive. This step-by-step manual guide covers force restarts, battery checks, and hardware fixes to restore normal operation.

steps.text:
Check charging cable and adapter:
Not all cables are created equal. A frayed, poor-quality, or worn Lightning or USB-C cable might look like it's charging while failing to actually deliver power.
The same goes for the adapter. To rule this out, try using a different Apple-certified or high-quality cable and adapter.

Ensure device is properly charged:
If the battery is completely drained, the iPhone needs a minimum charge before it can power on - sometimes up to 15-20 minutes.
You may see a low battery screen or nothing at all during this time, which is normal.

Try a different power source:
A laptop USB port or low-wattage adapter may not deliver enough power to a deeply drained battery.
Try plugging directly into a wall outlet with a Apple-certified adapter instead.

Force restart:
A force restart can revive a device that appears completely dead or unresponsive, and is also the go-to fix if the device won't turn off normally.
On iPhone 8 and later:
Quickly press and release Volume Up, quickly press and release Volume Down, then press and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears.

Check for physical damage:
Water damage or a cracked screen can prevent the display from showing anything, making the device appear off even when it isn't.
Look for signs of damage around the screen, ports, and buttons.
If the Side button is physically stuck or damaged, that along can prevent the normal power on/off behavior.

Check for iOS updates:
If the device powers on but constantly freezes or becomes unresponsive during shutdown, a software bug may be the cause.
notes:
Note: 

Go to Settings > General > Software Update and install any available updates.

steps.text:
Let the battery drain (can't turn off only):
If the device is frozen and won't respond to a force restart, leaving it until the battery fully drains will force it to shut off. Not ideal, but effective as a last resort before seeking repair.

tutorials.title: Using Spoken Content to read selected text or what's on your device's entire screen
tutorials.intro: Your device can say what's appearing on the screen out loud, and read selected text or suggested words while you're typing.

steps.text: From within the Settings app, scroll to and tap Accessibility.
Tap Read & Speak.
Tap Speak Selection to manage its settings.
notes:
Note: 

From this screen, tap or slide the Speak Selection switch to ON, then tap the Back icon to save your changes.

steps.text: Tap Speak Screen to manage its settings.
notes:
Note: 

From this screen, tap or slide the Speak Screen switch to ON, then tap the Back icon to save your changes.

steps.text: To use Speak Selection, touch and hold the text you would like your device to read out loud.
notes:
Note: 

You may also need to double-tap on the text to select it, and then adjust the selection criteria.

steps.text: Select Speak.
notes:
Note: 

Your device will begin dictating the selected text.

steps.text: To use Speak Screen, swipe down with two fingers from the top of the screen.
notes:
Note: 

Your device will begin dictating the content you see on your screen.

steps.text: You've completed the steps!

tutorials.title: Using emergency mode
tutorials.intro: Learn how to enter Emergency Mode on your device. You can access options such as Medical ID or Emergency SOS.

steps.text: From the Lock screen, press and hold either Volume button and the Side button simultaneously.
Slide the Emergency Call switch from left to right to call emergency services.
notes:
Note: 

By continuing to hold either Volume button and Side button, it will start a countdown that automatically calls emergency services upon your behalf.

steps.text: Access your emergency Contacts by sliding the Medical ID switch from left to right
You can tap an emergency contact’s number to call them directly.
notes:
Note: 

Emergency contacts will automatically be notified when you contact emergency services, as well as receive your current location.

tutorials.title: Using recovery mode
tutorials.intro: If you're having problems updating or restoring your device, you can enable recovery mode to restore or update with the assistance of your computer.

steps.text: Quickly press and release the Volume up button.
notes:
Note: 

For this tutorial, we're showing how to update iPhone using recovery mode. iTunes will try to reinstall iOS without deleting your data. You can choose to restore iPhone instead, but steps may vary based on what you choose.

steps.text: Quickly press and release the Volume down button.
Press and hold the Side button until you see the Apple logo.
Continue to hold the Side button and connect the device to your computer.
On your computer, click Update.
notes:
Note: 

After the update completes, follow the onscreen prompts to set up iPhone.

steps.text: You've completed the steps!

tutorials.title: What's New in iOS 27
tutorials.intro: Walkthrough the new features released with the latest OS update!

steps.text: Meet Siri AI
notes:
Note: 

Siri has been rebuilt into a conversational assistant that understands what's on your screen, searches across your messages, emails, and photos, and supports natural back-and-forth conversations. Say "Hey Siri," press the Side button, or swipe down from the Dynamic Island to get started. (Currently only available for users with a supported device set to English)

Say "Hey Siri," press the Side button, or swipe down from the Dynamic Island to get started. (Currently only available for users with a supported device set to English)

steps.text: Revisit conversations in the new Siri app
notes:
Note: 

Your Siri conversations now live in the dedicated Siri app and sync across your Apple devices with iCloud, so you can start a conversation on one device and continue it on another. (Currently only available for users with a supported device set to English)

steps.text: See what Siri sees with Siri mode
notes:
Note: 

Open Camera and use Siri mode to ask about objects seen through the camera. Siri can identify what you're looking at, answer questions, and provide relevant actions, such as getting nutrition information from food or helping split a bill. (Currently only available for users with a supported device set to English)

steps.text: Write with Siri anywhere you type
notes:
Note: 

Siri's Writing Tools can help draft, revise, and proofread text system-wide, including adjusting your writing based on context and how you typically communicate. (Currently only available for users with a supported device set to English)

steps.text: Try the new Photos editing tools
notes:
Note: 

Photos adds Spatial Reframing, Clean Up, and Extend. Reframe a photo and adjust its perspective, remove unwanted objects with Clean Up, or use Extend to generate more of the scene beyond the original image.

steps.text: Let Safari do more of the browsing for you
notes:
Note: 

Safari can automatically organize tabs into topics, use Notify Me to alert you when a webpage changes (such as a price drop or restock) and create custom extensions by describing what you want.

steps.text: Customize your look with Liquid Glass
notes:
Note: 

Go to Settings > Appearance to adjust the Liquid Glass look across your iPhone, including how clear or tinted the interface appears.

steps.text: Set independent alarm and alert volumes
notes:
Note: 

Under Settings > Sounds & Haptics, turn off Match Ringtone Volume to independently adjust Alarms and Timers and Alerts and System Sounds instead of tying them to your ringtone volume.

steps.text: Fix passwords with a tap
notes:
Note: 

The Passwords app can alert you to weak or compromised passwords and help update them on supported websites and apps.

steps.text: Explore new Child Safety tools
notes:
Note: 

iOS 27 introduces redesigned parental controls with several new ways to manage a child's device:

At-a-glance usage shows device usage and most-used apps.
Time Allowances set daily limits for categories such as Entertainment, Games, and Social Media.
Ask to Browse lets parents approve new websites.
Ask to Buy includes approval for app downloads.
Contact approval lets parents approve new contacts before a child can communicate with them.
Schedules control when apps and websites are available.
Always Allowed keeps selected apps and contacts accessible even when other access is paused.
